doc.title: Wendell Brunious interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Jerome Richardson and Father and Son
summary: He recalls Jerome Richardson's soprano playing on Gino Vannelli's record, which he and his father heard.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Yeah it was pretty seamless. I think it’s just Watrous. He just can hear man. That guy can — man can he play some sassy trombone. Boy that was such a great experience. Because Jerome was just — years and years ago he recorded a record, before CDs, an album with Gino Vanelli, where he played soprano.
With Gino Vanelli, get out, no kidding.

That’s Jerome playing that. I mean he was like playing some of the most incredible soprano I ever heard. You know my dad and I used to sit down — my dad died in ’76. So they must have recorded that around ’74, ’75. And I mean we used to sit around and listen to that and you know my dad being like a real staunch big band, swing type of guy you know, he would say hey man, that guy’s playing man, whoever it is. And I read the name, Jerome Richardson and I knew I’d heard it before. But that left a very lasting impression on me. And when I got to meet him, that was the first time I met him, when we came up there to record with you. And he was just such a great guy. It’s very nice to know that your heroes are nice people.
